description: Software supply chain security decomposed. SBOM (SPDX, CycloneDX). Sigstore (cosign, Rekor transparency log). SLSA framework levels. Reproducible builds. Dependency vulnerability scanning. Typosquatting + namespace attacks. The mechanisms by which downstream consumers verify upstream integrity.

sub_mechanisms.name: SBOM_inventory
sub_mechanisms.definition: List of components, versions, sources for a software artifact. SPDX or CycloneDX format.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inventory enables vulnerability response. Log4Shell: who has vulnerable log4j? SBOM answers immediately. US executive order 14028 mandates for federal software.

sub_mechanisms.name: SPDX_format
sub_mechanisms.definition: Linux Foundation SBOM standard. JSON/YAML/RDF. Standard fields for component identification + relationships.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cross-tool interoperability. License compliance use case + security. Slow to adopt but increasingly required.

sub_mechanisms.name: CycloneDX_format
sub_mechanisms.definition: OWASP SBOM standard. JSON/XML. Designed for security use case + machine readability.
sub_mechanisms.why: More security-focused than SPDX. Vulnerabilities, services, dependency relationships. Growing adoption.

sub_mechanisms.name: Sigstore_cosign
sub_mechanisms.definition: Open-source signing infrastructure for software artifacts. cosign signs container images, files. Free certificates via Fulcio CA.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lowers barrier to signing. OIDC-based identity (sign as your GitHub account). Adopted by Kubernetes, npm, PyPI.

sub_mechanisms.name: Rekor_transparency_log
sub_mechanisms.definition: Append-only public log of signatures. Cryptographic merkle tree. Detect compromised signing keys.
sub_mechanisms.why: Like Certificate Transparency for signatures. Public log means attacks visible. If your key signed something you didn't, log proves it.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLSA_level_1
sub_mechanisms.definition: Documented build process. Provenance of how artifact built.
sub_mechanisms.why: Baseline transparency. Foundation for higher levels. Most projects can achieve.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLSA_level_2
sub_mechanisms.why: Hosted CI (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) typically meets. Build platform itself trusted. Many open-source projects achieving.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLSA_level_3
sub_mechanisms.definition: Source + build platform meet security standards. Provenance non-forgeable.
sub_mechanisms.why: Higher bar. Requires hardened build infrastructure. Google, Microsoft major projects targeting.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLSA_level_4
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hermetic, reproducible builds. Two-party review of changes.
sub_mechanisms.why: Aspirational for most. Tor + Debian + Bitcoin Core target. Strongest guarantee but most cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: reproducible_builds
sub_mechanisms.definition: Same source produces byte-identical output regardless of who/when/where built.
sub_mechanisms.why: Allow third-party verification: 'I built from source, got same bytes — this binary matches source'. Debian + Tor pursuing. Hard but achievable.

sub_mechanisms.name: dependency_vulnerability_scanning
sub_mechanisms.definition: Automated tools comparing dependency versions to known CVEs. Snyk, Dependabot, Renovate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Massive automation. GitHub Dependabot opens PRs for vulnerable deps. Integration into dev workflow critical for keeping up with disclosed vulnerabilities.

sub_mechanisms.name: typosquatting
sub_mechanisms.definition: Publish malicious package with name similar to legitimate (request → reqeusts). Catches typos.
sub_mechanisms.why: Common npm + PyPI attack. Mitigation: package allowlists, automated detection (registry-side), code review.

sub_mechanisms.name: dependency_confusion
sub_mechanisms.definition: Internal package name unregistered on public registry. Attacker publishes; build tools prefer public version.
sub_mechanisms.why: Alex Birsan 2021: 35 major companies compromised. Mitigation: scoped namespaces, explicit registry config, private mirrors.

derivation_rules.name: SBOM_enables_rapid_vulnerability_response
then: SBOM enables instant query: which systems are affected
derivation_rules.why: Without SBOM: weeks of manual audit. With SBOM: SQL query against inventory. Log4Shell demonstrated need; industry now adopting.

derivation_rules.name: transparency_log_detects_signing_key_compromise
if: signatures are published to transparency log
derivation_rules.why: If attacker steals signing key + uses, log shows. Owner notices their key signed something they didn't. Same idea as Certificate Transparency for TLS certs.

derivation_rules.name: reproducible_builds_enable_third_party_verification
then: anyone can verify binary matches the source
derivation_rules.why: Without reproducibility, only build server knows. With it, anyone can rebuild + compare. Foundation of trust: 'don't trust me, trust the source you can verify'.

derivation_rules.name: dependency_confusion_via_namespace_collision
if: internal package name not registered publicly
then: attacker can register publicly + supply chain compromise occurs
derivation_rules.why: Build tools' precedence rules typically prefer higher version, often from public registry. Mitigation: register all internal package names publicly (defensive), scope namespaces, explicit registry config.

derivation_rules.name: SLSA_levels_provide_supply_chain_maturity_model
if: a project targets specific SLSA level
then: it has clear practices to implement and verify
derivation_rules.why: Maturity model approach. L1 documentation; L4 hermetic + reproducible. Concrete checklist. Google's Bcrypt + many CNCF projects publish their SLSA level.
